tagline: A coastal road connects cranberry country, working waterfronts and a lighthouse.
intro: SR 105 follows the Pacific coast through Grayland, then turns east near Twin Harbors State Park to trace the South Bay of Grays Harbor toward Aberdeen. The state designated it the Cranberry Coast Scenic Byway in recognition of cranberry growing. State of Washington Tourism now promotes the Aberdeen-to-Raymond corridor as Bay-2-Bay, a 50-mile journey connecting working waterfronts and coastal beaches.

The road began as the Aberdeen–Tokeland Highway, built in the 1920s to connect Westport and Tokeland with Aberdeen. It entered the state system in 1937, with a Westport spur and plans to extend to Raymond. Difficult terrain, soil and weather delayed that extension, which opened in 1962; the SR 105 number followed in 1964. Farther south, between Grayland and Tokeland, erosion from currents leaving Willapa Bay forced SR 105 inland from Cape Shoalwater in the 1990s. The coastal alignment has changed as well as its number.

For the Grayland-to-Aberdeen portion, travel north along the coast to Cohassett Beach. A four-mile spur continues north to Westport and the harbor mouth, with the Grays Harbor Lighthouse on Point Chehalis. Return to SR 105 for the drive east across the Elk and Johns rivers, through Ocosta and into Aberdeen, where Boone Street reaches US 101 on the Chehalis River’s southern bank.

moments.title: Grays Harbor Lighthouse
moments.text: Grays Harbor Lighthouse stands approximately 3,000 feet from high tide, although construction began in 1897 about 400 feet from the water’s edge. Land accumulated largely because of the harbor entrance’s jetty system. First lit in 1898, the tower rises 107 feet and marks the harbor entrance. Its brick walls have a cement coating. In 1992, a smaller light on the balcony replaced the original Fresnel lens in service; that older lens remains in the lantern room. The tower rests on a sandstone foundation twelve feet thick, with walls four feet thick at the base.

moments.title: Westport
moments.text: Westport’s marina holds a large commercial fishing fleet alongside recreational charter vessels. The town occupies the Point Chehalis Peninsula at the entrance to Grays Harbor from the Pacific. Its waterfront once had another connection across that entrance: a summer passenger ferry linked Westport to Ocean Shores until the service was discontinued in 2008. The road connection is the SR 105 spur, which winds through city streets before ending at the harbor. Cranberry farming remains a long-term part of the local economy, alongside the fishing port that occupies the harbor entrance.

moments.title: Bottle Beach State Park
moments.text: Tide flats make up most of Bottle Beach State Park on the southern shore of Grays Harbor. The 64-acre park has 6,000 feet of shoreline near the historic Ocosta townsite. Birding experts Bob Morse and Ruby Egbert urged its creation and donated money for land purchases in 1993. The park opened two years later, in 1995. Its Ruby Egbert Natural Area carries her name, and birdwatching, hiking and wildlife viewing are among the park’s activities.
